source.title: Representational Isomorphism and Alignment of Multilingual Large Language Models
source.authors: Di Wu; Yi-Bin Lei; Andrew Yates; Christof Monz

record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-language representational alignment with orthogonal Procrustes mapping and retrieval measures, rather than testing convergence across independently trained models as they scale.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many individual language-direction retrieval results. Rows below preserve the aggregate results stated in the text and selected direction-level results showing gains, failures, or dependence on settings; other matrix entries are noted under rows_left_out. The contrastive-training STS gains are excluded as rows because the alignment is deliberately induced by the training objective and STS performance is not itself a direct mapping or representation-similarity measure.
record.test_reason: The study measures whether sentence representations of different languages inside one LLM (LLaMA2, LLaMA3, BLOOM) can be aligned by an orthogonal Procrustes map. It never compares representations between independently trained models, across seeds, across modalities or across scale, which is what every version names. Within-model cross-lingual isomorphism is a related but different construct, so it is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test of V4, V6 or V7. The contrastive STS experiments deliberately induce alignment and are also out of scope.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also argue that English prompts already map non-English inputs into a shared English space, which is why the Procrustes gain shrinks there. They report that Tower's multilingual continued pretraining fails to align semantics, whereas representation-level contrastive alignment with about 100 pairs does.
record.recipe_differences: Uses multilingual sentence embeddings, orthogonal Procrustes mapping, and cross-lingual retrieval rather than reproducing either cited original source's method. The reported mappings are between language-specific representations from a model, not between independently trained models.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment and retrieval vary with prompt language (same-language versus English prompts), extraction method (prompting versus last-token pooling), Precision@1/@5/@10, language direction, and language resource level.

fits_no_version.finding: Within a single LLM, sentence embeddings for translation pairs in different languages are poorly aligned at first but become largely aligned after an orthogonal Procrustes rotation. Average P@5 rises from 0.25 to 0.71 for LLaMA2-7B, with similar gains for 13B, LLaMA3-8B and BLOOM. The gain is small or absent with English prompts, weak for low-resource languages, and weaker with last-token pooling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within one multilingual model, representations of different languages are near-isomorphic up to an orthogonal map, and the degree depends on prompt language, language resource level and pooling method.

record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
record.problems: The study tests representations across languages within model families rather than alignment between independently trained models or convergence with scale. It covers four model families and only a few languages in the STS analysis. Retrieval scores are reported without uncertainty estimates. Some directions show modest gains or decreases, especially with English prompts or low-resource languages.
record.rows_left_out: The retrieval matrices in Tables 1-2 and 4-14, plus Tables 16-17, report many additional language-direction values. The selected rows prioritize aggregate results and direction-level examples that show strong gains, incomplete gains, reversals, or sensitivity to settings; remaining matrix entries are omitted to keep the record concise. Table 3 and Table 15 report STS outcomes after contrastive fine-tuning with translation pairs; these are not extracted as evidence for uninduced convergence or simple mapping because the alignment is deliberately trained and the reported outcome is downstream STS performance.

untested.parts: No comparison of independently trained models, and no trend with scale.
No mapping between different models; the maps are only between languages inside one model.
No cross-model convergence measure whose metric or input dependence could be assessed.
No cross-model alignment level, plateau, or causal account.

record.verdict_notes: Direction labels in many rows appear to be transposed relative to the text's convention. The text cites EN⇒JA as 0.03 and EN⇒DE as 0.82, which are the first entries of the JA and DE columns, so direction-level values should be rechecked. The reader's labels for V4, V6 and V7 are withdrawn because no row measures alignment between different models.

versions.untested_parts: No test of whether alignment between independently trained models rises with model size or capability.
No comparison of training seeds, shared features, or seed-level subspaces.

Tests orthogonal linear mapping between language-specific representations from the same model, not mappings between independently trained models, stitched layers, relative representations, or unpaired-data mappings.
No test of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.

Tests dependence on retrieval precision setting, prompt language, pooling method, and language pair. Does not test neighbourhood settings beyond Precision@1, @5, and @10, or broad out-of-distribution conditions beyond the stated NTREX-to-Flores evaluation.
Tests incomplete and condition-dependent cross-language alignment. Does not establish a plateau or distinguish shared training data/objectives from a common model of reality as the cause.
